things.name: Gold ring
things.say: Gold is an element, number seventy-nine. Gold does not rust, so it stays shiny for a very long time. Most gold rings also have a little silver or copper mixed in to make them stronger.

box.title: What karat means
box.say: Pure gold is called twenty-four karat. Eighteen karat gold is eighteen parts gold and six parts other metals, like silver and copper.

things.name: Silver necklace
things.say: Silver is an element, number forty-seven. Over time silver can turn dark. That happens when it meets tiny amounts of sulfur in the air. This dark layer is called tarnish.

things.name: Pearls
things.say: A pearl grows inside an oyster or a mussel, layer by layer. It is made mostly of calcium carbonate, the same chemical as seashells.

things.name: Diamond
things.say: A diamond is made of carbon, the same element as the graphite in a pencil. Diamond is the hardest natural material.

box.title: Diamond and pencil
box.say: Pencil graphite and diamond are both carbon. In graphite the carbon is in flat layers that slide, so it is soft. In diamond the carbon holds on tight in every direction, so it is very hard.

things.name: Ruby
things.say: A ruby is a crystal of aluminium oxide. A tiny bit of chromium inside makes it red.

box.title: Ruby and sapphire
box.say: Ruby and sapphire are the same mineral, called corundum. A little chromium makes ruby red. A little iron and titanium make sapphire blue.

things.name: Emerald
things.say: An emerald is a mineral called beryl. It is made of beryllium, aluminium, silicon and oxygen. A little chromium makes it green.

things.name: Copper bracelet
things.say: Copper is an element, number twenty-nine. It is a reddish metal. Old copper slowly turns green on the outside, like the Statue of Liberty.
